edges: Central Area Command was formed by the Royal Australian Air Force during World War II.
No. 2 Group was re-formed as Central Area Command.
Air Commodore Adrian 'King' Cole was the inaugural Air Officer Commanding of Central Area Command.
Air Commodore Bill Anderson took over command of Central Area Command from Adrian 'King' Cole.
No. 2 (Training) Group was formed to take responsibility for training units under Central Area Command.
A proposal was made to carve a new Central Area Command out of Eastern Area.
The concept of a new Central Area Command was raised again in August 1944.
